declarations.description: A built-in mechanical predicate. Its verdicts are computed from the packet by fixed code, so a conviction verdict proves a task-level mechanical violation.
declarations.input_schema: body.predicate names a built-in predicate; body.output_verdicts must equal that predicate's full verdict vocabulary
declarations.name: deterministic

declarations.description: An inline typed-DSL program. Non-Turing-complete and interpreted by fixed operators, so it is deterministic and may hold conviction verdicts.
declarations.input_schema: body.predicate_definition carries a validated detector.predicate_program.v1 program whose name equals body.predicate
declarations.name: typed_dsl

declarations.description: A typed semantic judgment produced by an injected executor. Evidence only: it can never authorize a terminal conviction, and its artifact must be digest-pinned.
declarations.input_schema: body.predicate names the task schema the executor judges; body.output_verdicts must equal the semantic verdict vocabulary
declarations.name: typed_semantic

identity_mismatch: IV-1-001: the executor loaded artifact 'classifier-B' but the entry pins 'classifier-a'; refusing to attribute results to an artifact that did not produce them
no_executor: IV-1-001: typed_semantic needs an executor; none was supplied to this detection call. A learned judgment cannot be simulated by the deterministic default.
note: Offline: no provider call and no admission. Demonstrates the runner contract's enforcement, not detector quality.
unregistered_runner: IV-1-001: runner 'no_such_runner' is not registered; known runners are ['deterministic', 'typed_dsl', 'typed_semantic']
verdict_beyond_vocabulary: IV-1-001: semantic verdict 'convicted' is outside the declared vocabulary ['abstained', 'contradicted', 'supported']
